- When sentiment is 0.00 across recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >1.5% from prior day), model often overshoots in subsequent days; cap forecast at +1.0% above prior peak.
- If history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70.00), model tends to ignore it; adjust downward by 0.3–0.8% for next period.
- When sentiment is non-zero (even 0.20), model is more volatile; smooth forecast transitions by reducing standard deviation of 30d forecast by 15–20%.
- If true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), model may be overconfident; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30d horizon, model often overweights recent highs; use 10–15% weight decay on most recent 3 days in forecast smoothing.
